passage.text: Hundreds of thousands of Thais live in English-speaking countries.
passage.reading: ˈhʌndrədz əv ˈθaʊzəndz əv ˈtaɪz ˈlɪv ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˌspiːkɪŋ ˈkʌntriz.

passage.text: We talked to three of them about their lives abroad.
passage.reading: wiː ˈtɔːkt tə ˈθriː əv ðɛm əˈbaʊt ðɛr ˈlɪvz əˈbrɔːd.

passage.text: Aom, 45, moved to London twenty years ago.
passage.reading: ˈɔːm, ˈfɔːrti ˈfaɪv, ˈmuːvd tə ˈlʌndən ˈtwɛnti ˈjɪrz əˈɡoʊ.

passage.text: At first, she worked as a waitress, but now she owns two Thai restaurants.
passage.reading: ət ˈfɜːrst, ʃiː ˈwɜːrkt əz ə ˈweɪtrəs, bʌt ˈnaʊ ʃiː ˈoʊnz ˈtuː ˈtaɪ ˈrɛstərɑːnts.

passage.text: "Making a living in London isn't easy, because everything is so expensive," she says.
passage.reading: ˈmeɪkɪŋ ə ˈlɪvɪŋ ɪn ˈlʌndən ˈɪzənt ˈiːzi, bɪˈkɔːz ˈɛvriθɪŋ ɪz soʊ ɪkˈspɛnsɪv, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "But the British love Thai food, so business is good."
passage.reading: bʌt ðə ˈbrɪtɪʃ ˈlʌv ˈtaɪ ˈfuːd, soʊ ˈbɪznəs ɪz ˈɡʊd.

passage.text: Pong, 32, is a nurse at a hospital in Sydney.
passage.reading: ˈpɔːŋ, ˈθɜːrti ˈtuː, ɪz ə ˈnɜːrs ət ə ˈhɑːspɪtəl ɪn ˈsɪdni.

passage.text: He came to Australia as a student and decided to stay.
passage.reading: hiː ˈkeɪm tə ɔːˈstreɪljə əz ə ˈstuːdənt ənd dɪˈsaɪdɪd tə ˈsteɪ.

passage.text: "I have a permanent visa now, and next year I hope to become an Australian citizen," he says.
passage.reading: aɪ ˈhæv ə ˈpɜːrmənənt ˈviːzə ˈnaʊ, ənd ˈnɛkst ˈjɪr aɪ ˈhoʊp tə bɪˈkʌm ən ɔːˈstreɪljən ˈsɪtɪzən, hiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "I love the beaches here, but I miss my mom's cooking."
passage.reading: aɪ ˈlʌv ðə ˈbiːtʃɪz ˈhɪr, bʌt aɪ ˈmɪs maɪ ˈmɑːmz ˈkʊkɪŋ.

passage.text: Nok, 27, is a software engineer in Vancouver.
passage.reading: ˈnɔːk, ˈtwɛnti ˈsɛvən, ɪz ə ˈsɔːftwɛr ˌɛndʒɪˈnɪr ɪn vænˈkuːvər.

passage.text: Her parents were immigrants from Thailand, so she grew up in Canada.
passage.reading: hɜːr ˈpɛrənts wɜːr ˈɪmɪɡrənts frəm ˈtaɪlænd, soʊ ʃiː ˈɡruː ˈʌp ɪn ˈkænədə.

passage.text: "Vancouver is very diverse, and there are immigrants from all over the world," she says.
passage.reading: vænˈkuːvər ɪz ˈvɛri daɪˈvɜːrs, ənd ðɛr ər ˈɪmɪɡrənts frəm ˈɔːl ˈoʊvər ðə ˈwɜːrld, ʃiː ˈsɛz.

passage.text: "I'm a Canadian citizen, but I'm proud of my Thai culture, too."
passage.reading: aɪm ə kəˈneɪdiən ˈsɪtɪzən, bʌt aɪm ˈpraʊd əv maɪ ˈtaɪ ˈkʌltʃər, ˈtuː.

passage.text: Every summer, she visits her grandparents in Chiang Mai.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈsʌmər, ʃiː ˈvɪzɪts hɜːr ˈɡrænpɛrənts ɪn ˈtʃjɑːŋ ˈmaɪ.

passage.text: Their lives are very different, but all three of them still feel Thai in their hearts.
passage.reading: ðɛr ˈlɪvz ər ˈvɛri ˈdɪfərənt, bʌt ˈɔːl ˈθriː əv ðɛm ˈstɪl ˈfiːl ˈtaɪ ɪn ðɛr ˈhɑːrts.
